title: Volunteer coastguard application — known facts
description: Synthetic applicant profile plus previous conversation, covering every question for a Helensburgh volunteer coastguard application.

training.first_aid: Emergency first aid at work, renewed in 2025

known_facts.previous_conversation:
I want to apply to volunteer with the Coastguard Rescue Service at Helensburgh station, in Area 04: Inner Clyde to River Tay and east Scottish border. I live about eight minutes from the station by car. I have checked the membership information and believe I meet the eligibility criteria. I can attend the medical in November and all three advertised training blocks at Greenock Coastguard Station: 22–26 March 2027, 10–11 April 2027 and 1–2 May 2027.

I would like to volunteer because I have lived by the Clyde for years, enjoy sailing and walking along the coast, and want to help keep people safe in my local community. I work in maintenance coordination, where I follow safety procedures, organise equipment, communicate with different teams and stay calm when plans change. I have current first-aid training and would welcome the chance to develop specialist coastal rescue skills.

I have never volunteered with the Coastguard Rescue Service or worked for the Maritime and Coastguard Agency. I did volunteer with an RNLI shore team from 2021 to 2023. I helped with equipment checks and community water-safety events, rather than operational rescues. I stopped when I moved to Helensburgh and I am no longer involved with the RNLI.

I work Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm. I have discussed volunteering with my employer. They cannot routinely release me for call-outs during working hours, but have agreed that I can take leave for the scheduled Coastguard training. I am available on weekday evenings after work, at weekends during the day, and on weekend evenings. I do not normally work shifts and have no further recurring restrictions on those times.

conversation.content: Yes, I would like to go ahead with my volunteer coastguard application. Please use my details and what we discussed earlier.
